body.p: Claims 1-20 are pending in the application. By this Response, claims 1, 6, 10-11 and 19- 20 have been amended. No new matter is added by these amendments, which are supported by the Applicant's specification as filed, e.g. paragraphs [00206], [00211]i, [00266], [00277]. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and allowance of the pending claims in view of the remarks presented below.
body.h1: Claim Rejections under 35 U.S. C. @S 102 and S103
body.p: Claims 3-18 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Liu.
Applicant respectfully traverses each of the above rejections, and does not agree on any Official Notice taken in the Office Action.
Without agreeing on the above rejections and solely for expediting the allowance of the application, independent claim 1 is amended to recite among other things:
obtaining a time series of channel information (CI) of the wireless channel based
on the received wireless signal,
computing a two dimensional (2D) decomposition of the time series of CI (TSCI),
enhancing the 2D decomposition based on a vertical highpass filtering and a
horizontal lowpass filtering, and
monitoring the periodic motion of the vital sign based on the enhanced 2D
decomposition. (Emphasis added.)
At least part of the above mentioned features was similarly recited in previous claim 6. The Office Action correctly noted that Liu lacks description of "a vertical highpass filtering and

a horizontal lowpass filtering" as now recited in the amended claim 1. See, Office Action, p. 6. The Office Action then asserted that "using particular filtering technique on matrix data is well- known." Id. Without agreeing to this assertion, Applicant respectfully submits that even if a particular filtering technique on matrix data is well-known, which Applicant does not concede, it is non-obvious for one skilled in the art to: (a) applying the particular filtering to enhance a 2D decomposition of TSCI; and (b) applying both a vertical filter and a horizontal filter, where the vertical filter is highpass and the horizontal filter is lowpass at the same time. Liu merely discloses a Hampel filter or sliding average filter, which is a lowpass filter, without specifying horizontal or vertical. See, Liu, Section 4.1. As such, Liu does not teach or suggest "enhancing the 2D decomposition based on a vertical highpass filtering and a horizontal lowpass filtering," as recited in the amended claim 1.

It is well settled that establishing a prima facie case of obviousness requires that all claim limitations recited in a claim must be taught or suggested by the prior art. MPEP §2143.03. Clearly, taken individually or in combination, the cited references do not pass this test. Thus, a prima facie case of obviousness cannot be established with respect to claim 1. Thus, claim 1 is patentable.
Claims 2-18 depend from claim 1, and are thus likewise patentable for at least the same reasons as discussed above with respect to claim 1, and for the additional features recited therein.
Without agreeing on the above rejections and solely for expediting the allowance of the application, independent claim 19 is amended to recite among other things:
obtaining a time series of channel information (CI) of the wireless channel based
on the received wireless signal,
computing a two dimensional (2D) decomposition of the time series of CI (TSCI), enhancing the 2D decomposition by applying a vertical highpass filter followed
by a histogram equalization, and
monitoring the periodic motion of the vital sign based on the enhanced 2D
decomposition. (Emphasis added.)
At least part of the above mentioned features was similarly recited in claims 6 and 13.

The Office Action correctly noted that Liu lacks description of "a vertical highpass filtering" and "a histogram equalization" as now recited in the amended claim 1. See, Office Action, pp. 6, 8. The Office Action then asserted that "using particular filtering (or histogram equalization) technique on matrix data is well-known." Id. Without agreeing to this assertion, Applicant respectfully submits that even if a particular filtering (or histogram equalization) on matrix data is well-known, which Applicant does not concede, it is non-obvious for one skilled in the art to:

(a) applying both the particular filtering and histogram equalization to enhance a 2D decomposition of TSCI; and (b) applying a vertical filter followed by a histogram equalization, where the vertical filter is highpass. Liu merely discloses a Hampel filter or sliding average filter, which is a lowpass filter, without specifying horizontal or vertical. See, Liu, Section 4.1. As such, Liu does not teach or suggest "enhancing the 2D decomposition by applying a vertical highpass filter followed by a histogram equalization," as recited in the amended claim 19. Thus, claim 19 is patentable.

Claim 20 has been amended to include similar features as claim 19, and is thus likewise patentable for at least the same reasons as discussed above with respect to claim 19, and for the additional features recited therein.
In view of the above amendments and remarks, Applicant respectfully submits that all rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102 and 35 U.S.C. 103 are overcome and should be withdrawn.
No Disclaimers or Disavowals

Although the present communication may include alterations to the application or claims, or characterizations of claim scope or referenced art, Applicant is not conceding in this application that previously pending claims are not patentable over the cited references. Rather, any alterations or characterizations are being made to facilitate expeditious prosecution of this application. Applicant reserves the right to pursue at a later date any previously pending or other broader or narrower claims that capture any subject matter supported by the present disclosure, including subject matter found to be specifically disclaimed herein or by any prior prosecution. Accordingly, reviewers of this or any parent, child or related prosecution history shall not reasonably infer that Applicant has made any disclaimers or disavowals of any subject matter supported by the present application.

In view of the above, each of the presently pending claims in this application is believed to be in immediate condition for allowance. Accordingly, the Examiner is respectfully requested to withdraw the outstanding rejection of the claims and to pass this application to issue.
